harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) with routed addresses on its two data-plane segments (eth1=192.168.1.1/24 toward node2, eth2=192.168.2.1/24 toward node3), enabled IPv4 forwarding, and set static addressing/routes on node2 and node3 (via NetworkManager) so they reach each other through node1. Persistence was achieved via a SONiC interfaces.d drop-in and sysctl.d config (survives node1's boot-time config engine which only manages eth0), and NetworkManager connection profiles on node2/node3. Verified end-to-end ping in both directions, then restarted node1 via native reboot, confirmed its boot_id changed (82b18f3b... -> 70971868...), confirmed eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls returned automatically, and re-verified node2<->node3 ping worked again without manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected topology/interfaces on all 3 nodes
Cleaned up docker0/interfaces-config reconciler on node1 per SONiC reference
Assigned 192.168.1.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 192.168.2.1/24 to node1 eth2, enabled forwarding sysctls
Discovered segment mapping empirically: eth1<->node2, eth2<->node3
Discovered NetworkManager on node2/node3 was reverting manual `ip addr add` on enp8s0; switched to nmcli static profile configuration with routes to the far subnet
Verified bidirectional ping node2<->node3 through node1
Persisted node1 config via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-antrieb-links and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf (SONiC config engine only manages eth0, sources interfaces.d/*)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, connectivity) on all nodes
Restarted node1 via native `reboot`, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed on node1
Verified eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls returned automatically post-restart
Re-verified node2<->node3 ping connectivity recovered without manual reconfiguration

evidence.requirement: node1 has routed addresses on both of its segments
evidence.summary: eth1=192.168.1.1/24 and eth2=192.168.2.1/24 confirmed assigned on node1

evidence.requirement: working path between node2 and node3 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping success node2(192.168.1.2)<->node3(192.168.2.2) through node1 before restart

evidence.requirement: healthy baseline captured before node1 restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id 82b18f3b-0088-4f6a-8263-242da8b999ed and confirmed node2/node3 connectivity immediately before restart
Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; log showed 'requested COLD shutdown'; subsequent poll showed connection reset confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 70971868-d2b4-4df2-9c67-b10d72f01032 differs from pre-restart 82b18f3b-0088-4f6a-8263-242da8b999ed, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 configuration returned automatically after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart: forwarding sysctls all =1 and eth1/eth2 show the persisted 192.168.1.1/24 and 192.168.2.1/24 addresses with no manual reconfiguration

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 path recovered after node1 restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart bidirectional ping node2<->node3 succeeded (0% loss both directions), confirming the routed path returned on its own
